explainer: The single best AI-bubble bellwether is the rental price of an installed Nvidia GPU, measured in dollars per GPU-hour, and specifically the H100: it is the daily marginal clearing price for AI compute, it is published by independent indexes (Silicon Data's SDH100RT, SemiAnalysis's one-year contract index), and a CME futures contract on it is pending: the CFTC extended its review to November 9, 2026, so a forward curve is coming but not yet listed. Right now it is saying the opposite of discounting: the Silicon Data index sits at $2.75/hr (Sep 30), a new high, one-year contract rates rose about 40% from $1.70 to $2.35 between October 2025 and March 2026, spot has run at roughly twice contract, and a four-year-old chip is renting for more than it did a year ago while CoreWeave says it has contracted 2020-vintage GPUs out to 2029 at full price. Pair it with three things: neocloud credit spreads (CoreWeave's July loan cleared at SOFR+550 for a 10.44% yield with maintenance covenants, and its CDS implies roughly a coin-flip default probability), which is the financing leg and the one signal already flashing red; server DRAM and HBM contract-price momentum (+13-18% QoQ in 3Q26 after +93-98% in 1Q26, with 4Q26 guided to only +3-8%), because memory is the first physical input that will roll over; and hyperscaler backlog growth versus capex growth (Microsoft commercial RPO +84%, Oracle RPO +363%, roughly $2.4 trillion of committed cloud backlog against about $1 trillion of 2026 capex), because the bubble only deflates if the buyers stop signing. Over the next one to two quarters watch Nvidia's August 26 print for gross margin and customer concentration (three direct customers were already 54% of revenue), the shape of the CME H100/B200 curve if the CFTC clears it in November (a steep backwardation would be the first public forecast of discounting), whether 4Q26 memory contract talks and 2027 HBM4 pricing turn negative, and what ERCOT's December audit says about how much of Texas's 474 GW interconnection queue is phantom demand. The threshold that would flip the call is simple: the H100 index sustained below about $2.00/hr, or spot trading below the one-year contract rate, while Blackwell and Rubin volumes keep arriving; until then compute is being sold at a premium, not a discount, and the risk lives in who is borrowing to build it rather than in the price of the product.

indicators.name: B200 rental price, $/GPU-hour (Silicon Data index) and B200/H100 ratio

As with H100, the 7-day percentages jumped (B200 +1.2% to +4.0%, B300 +2.5% to +6.3%) without a matching price move, so treat them as a base-week effect. The FAQ's stale $5.45 is ignored and there is no CME/CFTC news. ASML said Wednesday that planned 2027-28 tool supply will not fully meet AI demand, which supports a tight Blackwell/Rubin market. Trend and signal held; watch TSMC's Thursday guide and any Rubin timing.

indicators.value: A100 index $1.52 Oct 13 (+3.8% 7d; trigger $1.50), up 1c and two cents above the floor. H200 $3.38, up 3c. Silicon Data residual study (Jan 30 data): used H100 ~65-75% of new at 2 yrs, 45-55% at 3 yrs; low end $12-16K. No new impairments Oct 13-14.

No used-H100 price reports, impairments or useful-life changes were found Oct 13-14, so the residual-study ranges are carried forward. A print under $1.50 would still move the signal to neutral. Watch it daily and in Q3 results from late October.

indicators.name: Power bottleneck: ERCOT/PJM queues, Texas permit freeze, turbine backlog
indicators.value: FERC (Oct 9 order) rejected PJM's interim large-load service, which let data centres connect without new capacity if curtailable, and its bring-your-own-capacity rules; approved the large-load definition and registry. ERCOT 474 GW large-load queue; TCEQ freeze since Sep 21, report Oct 19; TWDB report Oct 14.
indicators.why: Grid capacity is still the binding constraint on how fast compute can be deployed: PJM is issuing tight-conditions advisories in October and only just fast-tracking its first new generators, which keeps existing GPU capacity scarce.
indicators.watch: Texas TWDB report Oct 14 and TCEQ compliance report Oct 19; PJM's revised large-load filing after FERC's Oct 9 rejection; ERCOT Batch Zero timing; GE Vernova Q3 backlog (late Oct).
indicators.note: No new reading since Oct 13: no Texas, ERCOT, PJM or turbine news was found for Oct 13-14, and the Texas Water Development Board's data-centre report due Oct 14 was not yet published in search results. The FERC rejection of PJM's interim large-load service (Oct 9) remains the latest change and keeps the quickest route for new AI load onto PJM shut for now. Trend and signal held. Watch the TWDB report, PJM's next filing and TCEQ's compliance report Oct 19.

indicators.name: Capex vs backlog: hyperscaler spend, RPO, AI-lab commitments and buyer revenue quality
indicators.value: ASML Q3 (Oct 14): sales EUR 11.66B, a hair under consensus; GM 57.5%; Q4 guide EUR 14.2-15.2B; 2026 raised to EUR 44-45B. Says planned 2027-28 supply will not meet demand; some customers asking for 2029-30 slots. OpenAI run-rate 'approaching $50B' (FT) vs ~$70B assumed.
indicators.why: Equipment demand says the build keeps accelerating, but the biggest buyer's revenue base is ~30% smaller than the market assumed, so backlog coverage by customer revenue got worse on paper; it is an accounting gap, not a demand drop, which keeps this neutral rather than bearish.
indicators.watch: Anthropic investor session Oct 14 (US); OpenAI's $30B round at $1.4T pre-money closing or re-priced; TSMC capex guide Thu 17:00 AEDT; Q3 hyperscaler capex guides late Oct.
indicators.note: Changed since Oct 13: ASML's Q3 is the strongest capex signal this week. CEO Christophe Fouquet said customers keep raising forecasts 'driven primarily by their expectations for the scale and duration of AI-related investments', that planned 2027-28 supply will fall short, and that ASML is looking beyond its planned 30% capacity increase for 2028 (Yahoo). ASML no longer reports quarterly bookings, and its US shares fell about 3% overnight on the small sales miss. This shows supplier-side capex rising, but it says nothing new about whether buyers' revenue covers the spend, so trend and signal held. No OpenAI round or Anthropic update was found Oct 13-14; watch Anthropic (Wed US) and TSMC (Thu 17:00 AEDT).
